sections.title: Portfolio Construction & Pareto Principle
sections.content:
The Pareto Principle (80/20 rule) drives portfolio construction: 20% of focused efforts generate 80% of results. Theme-based investing centers on AI as the overarching narrative, with different stocks requiring different management approaches based on position size and conviction.

Position sizing follows strict tiers: 2.5% for exploratory positions, 5% for good stocks with channel trading opportunities, and 10% for positions with clear edge or hedging capability. Heavy allocations (8-9%) on core conviction plays like Meta require hawk-like monitoring, while smaller positions can be managed more passively.

![Figure: Portfolio allocation framework showing position sizing tiers](frame:periodic_0002.jpg)

The instructor's growth portfolio achieved 41% absolute return (47% in INR terms) over 11 months, representing 3x outperformance versus the 13% Nasdaq benchmark. With systematic options integration, minimum safe returns of 6% annually are achievable, potentially reaching 55-56% total returns.

Profit-taking methodology involves booking 20-25% of positions when achieving significant gains (230%+ example with EOS stock) to recover initial principal, allowing the remainder to run with reduced psychological burden.

sections.title: Baseline Returns & Trend Analysis Framework
sections.content:
Baseline return establishment is critical before deploying capital. NASDAQ averages 17-18% annually in dollar terms, while Indian small/mid-cap averages 16-17% annually. The framework involves three steps: establish baseline return, identify current trend trajectory, and project forward returns if trend continues.

![Figure: QQQ trend analysis chart showing weekly candlestick pattern with trend lines and return projections](frame:periodic_0123.jpg)

Euphoria detection occurs when retail investors and non-professionals discuss assets with conviction, but this is NOT a timing signal for exit. The bubble burst paradox states that when consensus recognizes a bubble exists, it's unlikely to burst immediately. Historical evidence shows that waiting for "obvious" crashes results in missed gains.

Market corrections are more likely than catastrophic crashes. The 2020-2021 NASDAQ rally of 78-79% in 1.5-2 years was euphoric versus the 17-18% baseline, leading to the 40% correction in 2022. Gold analysis across multiple timeframes shows euphoria on 1, 3, and 5-year bases but baseline returns on 10-year basis.

sections.title: Magnificent Seven Market Analysis & Support Levels
sections.content:
The Magnificent Seven stocks serve as market health indicators. When all major stocks top simultaneously, it signals euphoria. Currently, 6 of 7 major stocks are down 11-21% from peaks, indicating an incomplete market top with bullish setup potential.

Microsoft shows -15% drawdown, Meta -20%, Apple -11 to -15%, Broadcom -21%, while Google remains at all-time highs. This pattern suggests significant upside potential remains, as market tops require near-universal participation in peak formation.

![Figure: Microsoft technical chart showing trend channels and support levels](frame:periodic_0272.jpg)

The fundamental analysis framework requires three assessments: revenue growth (is total revenue increasing?), profit generation (are operating profits growing at reasonable pace?), and capital efficiency with ROIC >12-13% as the benchmark for American companies. Broadcom demonstrates this with 17% ROIC and 3x operating profit expansion over 4 years.

Forward P/E ratios account for expected earnings growth over 3-9 months, compressing as earnings expand. Five to six macroeconomic drivers support forward earnings: midterm elections, Trump tax break timing, GDP growth acceleration, unemployment levels, market liquidity, and political incentives to maintain elevated markets.

sections.title: Position Sizing & Margin of Safety Strategy
sections.content:
Margin of safety is non-negotiable—never buy assets at all-time highs without discount. Position sizing must match conviction: 2.5% for exploratory positions, 5% for good stocks with channel trading opportunity, and 10% for positions with clear edge or hedging capability.

The 5% stock strategy involves starting with 2.5% position at initial entry, adding another 2.5% if stock falls (total 5%), with room to average down while maintaining discipline. Once both tranches are deployed, do NOT add more positions on further declines to avoid Cathie Wood-style ego-driven averaging.

![Figure: Channel trading pattern showing support and resistance levels for systematic entry/exit](frame:periodic_0430.jpg)

Channel trading requires buying at support levels and exiting at resistance systematically. The pattern shows stocks oscillating between support and resistance with multiple touches confirming the channel. Entry occurs at the lower band, exit at the upper band, with 2.5% initial position and 2.5% addition if support holds.

Quality company assessment focuses on business model, profit margins, and network effects. MasterCard exemplifies this with strong business model, high margins, and network effects creating a tradeable channel over 4+ years with consistent bounces between $470-$480 support and $620-$630 resistance.

sections.title: Protective Put Strategy for Mastercard & Visa
sections.content:
The protective put strategy combines long stock positions with put options to create defined risk/reward profiles. For Mastercard/Visa positions, buy stock at market price (~$530) and purchase put options at $520 strike as downside protection, with position sizing of $50,000 per stock.

Political risk from Trump administration's potential 10% credit card interest rate cap serves as the catalyst. Current rates of 32-33% would make 10% caps unprofitable for banks, likely killing the market. Congress is unlikely to approve due to economic damage, making the threat likely to be dismissed.

![Figure: Risk-reward diagram showing protective put payoff structure](frame:periodic_0617.jpg)

The risk-reward profile offers unlimited upside if stock rises above $530, with downside capped at 4-6% (insurance premium cost). The 6-month target of 17-20% return annualizes to 34-40%, significantly outperforming the 16-17% market benchmark.

Strike price selection ($520) is based on maximum acceptable loss tolerance, representing a 1.9% buffer below entry price. Only execute this strategy on stocks with sensible/low option premiums—never apply to high-volatility stocks like Nebius, Iron, ASTS, or Rocket Lab where premiums are prohibitively expensive.

sections.title: Collar Strategy & Advanced Options Techniques
sections.content:
The collar strategy combines protective puts with covered calls to create asymmetric payoff profiles. For Meta, buy 100 shares at ~$650, purchase put at $630 (4% OTM) costing ~11%, and sell call at $850 (30% OTM) collecting 5% premium.

Net position calculation: Put cost (-11%) + Call premium (+5%) = Net downside (-6%), with upside potential of +33%, creating a 5.5:1 risk-reward ratio. Account size requirements are $300,000 minimum for Mastercard setup and $500,000 minimum for Meta setup.

![Figure: Collar strategy payoff diagram showing limited downside and capped upside](frame:periodic_0860.jpg)

Stock selection criteria focus on mid-to-low volatility ranges. Avoid high-volatility stocks like Nvidia that require constant monitoring. The strategy works best with stable, predictable price action where different strategies are needed for high-volatility names.

Time horizon uses 1-year expiries for collar strategies with expected exit in 6 months. The framework allows flexibility: "The sooner this happens, the better it is for us." If stock moves sideways, close put and call options by buying back sold positions and selling back bought positions.

sections.title: Covered Calls & Monopoly Company Investing
sections.content:
Covered call strategies on Nifty 50 involve selling 5% out-of-the-money monthly call options when clear trading ranges are established. Expected returns range from 8-12% annually if market maintains range-bound behavior, though this underperforms the 17-18% market growth expectation.

Monopoly company identification focuses on businesses with sustainable competitive advantages. Netflix qualifies through synonymous brand association with entertainment, high customer retention, and pricing power. Visa/Mastercard demonstrate true monopoly characteristics with flywheel effects where increased merchant usage spreads fixed costs across more users.

![Figure: Nifty 50 chart showing range-bound trading suitable for covered call strategy](frame:periodic_1128.jpg)

Position sizing rules maintain 5% maximum allocation for quality monopoly companies (Amazon, Netflix, Microsoft, Google, Meta), with 2.5% allocation for high-risk/high-reward positions like Duolingo that could become multi-baggers or go to zero.

Buying mistakes to avoid include purchasing at all-time highs with zero margin of safety and not buying corrections. The instructor's philosophy: avoid both mistakes by not buying monopoly companies at peaks and buying more when they fall, positioning for recovery and compounding.

Entry timing rules prohibit selling call options when Nifty is at all-time highs. Wait for 5% correction before initiating covered call strategies, ensuring clear ranges are established before deploying options income strategies.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
• **Position sizing discipline**: Use 2.5%, 5%, and 10% tiers based on conviction and hedging capability—never exceed without clear edge
• **Margin of safety is non-negotiable**: Only buy quality companies at 20-25% discounts, never at all-time highs
• **Protective puts enable larger positions**: 4-6% insurance cost converts risk profiles to asymmetric payoffs with unlimited upside
• **Collar strategies require $300K+ accounts**: Combine puts and calls for 5:1+ risk-reward ratios on mid-volatility stocks only
• **Baseline returns guide deployment**: Establish 17-18% annual expectations before capital allocation; deploy on 10% corrections
• **Magnificent Seven as market health indicator**: 6 of 7 stocks down 15-20% suggests incomplete top with upside potential
• **Options income strategies**: Systematic covered calls and cash-secured puts can generate 12% annual yields vs 5-6% passive dividends
• **Geographic diversification**: Favor US markets for growth and options access; maintain minimal Indian allocation due to INR weakness
• **Cash reserves are hedges**: Maintain 15-20% cash for investors without options access; deploy on market dips
• **Quality over speculation**: Focus on monopoly businesses with network effects and pricing power for long-term compounding
